page.layout: One printed page: running head at top, text block in the centre and right with margin notes in the left margin.; One column of running text, centred-left on the scan, with short partly printed marginal notes in the left margin. Notes at the left edge of the column. Below the last line of text, at the right, one catchword. Nothing else on this scan is printed text.

main_text.p: o Li[?] Ciuil[?] 22.c[?]p In[?] in ill[?] locu[?]q Li[?] c ip[?] ignibus meruerunt dari? cur immaniter conventicula dirui, in quibus oratur Deus, pax cunctis & venia postulatur, Magi-stratibus, Exercitibus, Regibus? Audi Minutium Felicem, Arnobij coætaneum in suo Dialogo, qui Octavius inscribitur, quot ex nostris, non dextram solùm, sed totum corpus vri, cremari, sine vl-lis ejulatibus pertulerunt, cùm dimit-ti præsertim haberent in sua poteftate? Imo{°} S. Augustinum audi, de his ipsis temporibus perorantem, neque tum civi-b.det.Deiap.tas Christi, quamuis adhuc peregrinaretur in terris, & haberet tam magnorum agmi-na populorum, aduersus impios persecuto-res suos pro temporali salute pugnauit: sed potiùs vt obtineret æternam, non repugna-uit; Audi denique {r}Ludouicum Viuem in hæc Augustini verba ita commentan-Com.umtem; [ obsistere poterant, & captis ar-m.mis non modò inimicis metum facere; sed periculum adferre, se propulsando, cæterùm longè beatius, & Euangelio Christi dignius existimabant iniuriam pati quàm facere; mori quàm occidere, corpus amit-tere, quàm animam.] Vnius tamen me-ib.8.minit ex {q}Eusebio{r} Nicephorus hominis

page.notes: Only the left margin notes are legible. Their right-hand parts are not readable, so the fragments end where the visible letters stop. Left margin notes are only partly printed; the visible fragments are copied as they stand: "b.de", "t.Dei", "ap.", "Com.", "um", "m.", "ib.8.", and a further fragment "r 6.5." at the foot of the margin. Reference marks ° (after Imo), r (before Ludouicum), q (before Eusebio) and r (before Nicephorus) are read from the scan. The left-hand portion of the column line beginning "ignibus" is a fragment and is transcribed as such. Italic and roman boundaries within the lines are read from the scan and may be imprecise where the type is worn.
